204fd7a0b86399254d63d96216fb64ecdb141e3e: Le Lac Blanc is a low-key resort on a modest scale: 14 km of runs for an intimate skiing experience, far from the bustle of the big resorts. This is where you come for calm, authenticity and no queues at the lifts. The family reputation of Le Lac Blanc is well deserved: dedicated beginner areas, well-groomed green runs and a friendly atmosphere at the foot of the lifts. It is one of the most reassuring resorts in the Vosges for laying the foundations of skiing with children. The modest altitude of Le Lac Blanc, starting at 900 m with the summit at 1200 m, makes it sensitive to climate variations. January and February remain the safest months for optimal snow cover. Outside that window, checking the snow reports before you leave is strongly advised. With a day lift pass at just 20€, Le Lac Blanc is one of the most affordable destinations in France. For families on a tight budget, or skiers who want to fit in plenty of days without breaking the bank, it is a sincere and often overlooked choice. In short: Le Lac Blanc doesn't rival the giants of skiing, and doesn't pretend to. It is an honest destination, often underrated, that deserves to be (re)discovered.
205199cfb271944cc2ddda97ff2641ef0f09392b: Livigno offers 115 km of well-marked runs — a mid-sized ski area ideal for spending 4 to 5 days without ever skiing exactly the same thing twice. The 32 lifts are generally sufficient to cope with queues in high season. Livigno has kept an authentic mountain village identity, far from the concrete resorts of the 1970s. People come here for the fresh air, unspoilt scenery and a friendly atmosphere that contrasts with the industrialisation of skiing in some large ski areas. With a summit at 2798 m and a village at 1816 m, snow reliability in Livigno is generally good from January to the end of March. A few exceptionally mild winters can cause snow shortages early in the season, but the situation recovers quickly once serious snowfalls arrive. A stay in Livigno is clearly expensive: 72€ for a day lift pass, plus accommodation and mountain restaurants among the most expensive in the Alps. It's the price of excellence — but be aware of it before you go. In short: Livigno lives up to its promises. A Northern Alps resort that will suit most profiles without disappointing.
